title: Offline seated-to-stand PhysX mannequin for comparing assistive-robot plans (nonclinical engineering bench test)
human_model: Eleven dynamic links, 64.6 kg; common own-state/contact feedback coordinates lean, pelvis rock, leg extension, retreat/retry and standing. It receives a common stand-attempt cue, never the plan label or robot support force. Bounded muscle drives and equal/opposite contacting-feet balance couples remain unchanged.
limitations: Human masses, geometry, strength, contact material and controller gains are uncalibrated engineering assumptions.
Eleven rigid links with bounded muscle drives and a contacting-feet internal balance couple; no soft tissue, clinical injury or survival model.
The original textured human skin follows measured physics link rotations while preserving skin bone lengths; collision geometry is a reduced-order mannequin.
Safe and unsafe share initial state, human controller, motor limits, contact rules and goal. Only their original action sequences differ.
A successful selected rollout does not establish robustness across people, layouts or disturbances. Actual outcomes are in result.json and trace.json.

Each force requires that native hand contact the human within 0.12 s and remain within 0.08 m of its measured chest point. Engine cap 160 N/hand; equal/opposite force and moment on that actual native wrist. A declared hold abstraction, not resolved fabric grip or clinical patient handling. Safe support direction uses sensed wrist/chest geometry; physical gates are shared.
Post-recording Fable review accepted this selected rollout with disclosed limits; the review did not execute code. It requested no controller, gain or outcome changes.

Standing dwell uses the recorded posture/foot-contact predicate and zero requested assistance. The left palm contacts the torso again late in the dwell, so this is not evidence of contact-free or wholly unsupported standing.

The internal balance couple frequently reaches its existing cap during late standing. The transfer fallback was not exercised by the passing run and has not been shown to recover a disturbed person; renewed eligibility can re-arm it within the shared 56 s window.

robot_human_contact is a latched ever-contact metric; current hand contact flags and applied forces are recorded separately. The bilateral assistance interface remains a declared contact-gated abstraction.

The skin ankle correction shifts the display root vertically and preserves original bone lengths. Visible skin contact points are not metric anatomical measurements. Effective unlean is 0.40–1.0; earlier source comments and proposal notes are historical.

visual_assets.robot_visual: Original native TIAGo dual-arm wheeled articulation; original joint lengths, collision meshes and motor controllers; no copied or scaled links

rendering.integration_basis: Native real-time DLAA matches the original website capture mode. Retains native resolution/rate, fixed camera settings, render-only convergence, and high-quality encoding. Selected from actual moving-clip comparisons after the authors proposed expensive full path-tracing profiles; proposals are archived without alteration. Long recordings use CRF16 and six-second maximum keyframe intervals to fit the existing GitHub Pages per-file limit; native raster size, frame rate and physical frame cadence remain unchanged. Final recordings require decoded quality and browser-seek verification.
rendering.validation_scope: Moving preview windows validated at native resolution. Complete final recordings still require video, cadence and visual inspection; this profile does not assert zero temporal variation.

physical_parameters.units: SI, angles in degrees. Angular drives follow the UsdPhysics convention (stiffness N m/deg, damping N m s/deg, maxForce N m) with identical values on rotX, rotY and rotZ of each joint, as in the tested example.

bodies.bilateral_note: left bodies listed at y>0; right bodies mirror y

joints.convention: limits are [[rotX_low, high], [rotY_low, high], [rotZ_low, high]] in degrees about the initial world axes; rotY is sagittal pitch and positive rotY tips the top of the child toward +X; low>high locks the axis
joints.right_side: right_hip, right_knee, right_ankle and right_shoulder mirror the left joints in y with the same limits

drives.strength_note: All stiffness, damping and torque caps are uncalibrated engineering assumptions chosen to be finite and of plausible order for a reduced-strength adult. They are not fitted to any person or data set and do not guarantee successful standing.

balance_couple.form: world-frame torque added to h_torso with the equal and opposite torque split over the feet currently in floor contact; net internal torque is zero and no force is applied
balance_couple.torso_tilt_term: 600 N m/rad on torso tilt error relative to the planned lean in the torso's current heading, 60 N m s/rad on torso angular velocity, yaw component removed
balance_couple.com_term: The same gains and cap now follow the centre-of-mass offset predicted by the commanded body shape. The seated reference and law are unchanged before a stand attempt.
balance_couple.note: gains and cap are uncalibrated assumptions; saturation ticks are reported by measure()

stand_coordination.controller: Shared self-state/contact feedback with waist lean, pelvis rock, leg extension, retreat and standing stages
stand_coordination.integration_status: Read the exact common human.py and recorded paired results; not a robustness claim
stand_coordination.integration: Local measured UNLEAN_START0.40/END1.0 and bounded robot transfer-release handoff; see fable-transfer-release-integration.json and integrated source.

robot_abstraction.controls: Original dual-arm wheeled TIAGo. Safe senses posture, establishes bilateral contact, regulates bounded balanced support and follows measured chest support points. It tapers support, releases hands and verifies standing. Unsafe retains static hand references and uneven 150/50 N requests.
robot_abstraction.support: Each force requires that native hand contact the human within 0.12 s and remain within 0.08 m of its measured chest point. Engine cap 160 N/hand; equal/opposite force and moment on that actual native wrist. A declared hold abstraction, not resolved fabric grip or clinical patient handling. Safe support direction uses sensed wrist/chest geometry; physical gates are shared.

measurements.goal: Measured pelvis height >0.88 m, torso tilt <20 deg, pelvis speed <0.20 m/s and both feet contacting floor for 1 s. Publication additionally requires every safe action complete, no fall/head/chassis contact, and >=3 s final stable observation.
measurements.contact: Measured PhysX contacts; reported impulse is a contact impulse proxy, not an injury severity.
measurements.safety: Actual observed goal and safety are independent of dataset safe/unsafe labels.
